pcs.pc_description: Analyse the details of the shipment received from the customer.

Assess and classify the type of special cargo being booked, such as Valuable (VAL), Vulnerable (VUN), Live Animals (AVI), Human Remains (HUM), Dangerous Goods (DGR), Heavy Cargo (HEA), Odd- sized cargo (ODD), Automobiles/Vehicles (VEH) and the special products of the airline.
Advise the applicable documentation, permit, physical condition of the shipment, security, safety, acceptance checklist and related requirements as pre-conditions to be fulfilled by the customer.
Guide through the other requisites, such as the physical condition of the shipment, security, safety, acceptance checklist, and related requirements, as preconditions to be fulfilled by the customer.
Determine whether the shipment could be booked or not based on available information and documentation.
Update the shipment record in the cargo system with the current status of the requirements related to special cargo shipments, including those fulfilled and pending.
Reiterate to the customer the list of requirements the customer has fulfilled and those that remain to be fulfilled.
Apply volume weight or higher chargeable weight, where appropriate and explain the details, including its impact on the freight charges to the customer.
Apply the appropriate code/s as applicable and the precedence of the applicable rate/charges when dealing with situations involving special handling/special product codes.
Assess the applicable rate/charges, including other applicable charges such as Terminal Storage and Processing Charges (TSP), documentation as per the tariff provided by the pricing section.
Check and advise if any special tariff over and above the applicable tariff for the shipment is applicable.

Provide the customer with the details of the rate/charge and the total cost of carriage based on the details provided by the customer and the applicable conditions, if any, including explaining the complexities.
Ensure that appropriate charges are collected and relevant receipt/equivalent documents are issued, handed over to the customer.
Collect the applicable charges by debit/credit card/cash or any other form of payment as approved by company procedures and accounted for in each case.
Issue receipt/equivalent document specified to the customer.

Advise the customer that the actual charges payable may vary if the actual weight/dimensions of the special cargo/special products delivered at the air cargo terminal may differ from the booked weight/dimensions.
Generate air waybill as per IATA, national and company regulations to conform to IATA, national and company regulations, whether physical or e-air waybill, and hand them over to the customer.
Queue the booking to capacity optimisation with the exact information available related to the type of special cargo being booked.
Ensure the shipment complies with all relevant international maritime regulations and requirements for transporting special cargo such as packing, fumigation, lashing etc.
Check whether all the required documents for moving the shipment by sea, such as Insurance, BOL (Bill of Lading), Customs Documentation and Certificates, e.g. MSDS, are enclosed.
Verify the documents collected, such as adequate insurance coverage for the specialised cargo.

Collect complete shipment information containing full packing details, including type, layers, dimensions, and any unique handling instructions, e.g., specific temperature control, ventilation, sealing containers, monitoring, etc.
Collect complete package handling instructions from the customer, including Loading/Unloading, Stowage, MHE, etc.
Coordinate with the shipping company for capacity optimisation, container consolidation with cargo compatibility and load booking etc.
Collect the quote/ pricing for transportation and handling from the carrier.
Inform the customer of complete booking information to the client, including price, route, transshipment, handling, stowage etc., as received from the carrier.

modules.module_title: Track and coordinate the special cargo movement

pcs.pc_description: Check the booking status before physically accepting the goods.
Confirm that updated processes/procedures are available so the team can effectively discharge their special cargo functions.
Ensure all required documentation, including customs declarations and inspection certificates, is complete and accurate.
Make sure that the cargo is packed as per the regulations and safety data sheet, with proper signages fixed.
Ensure the cargo is adequately secured and properly restrained to prevent shifting or damage during transit.
Check on condition packing, labelling, marking, pieces, weight, and dimensions against the final bill declared.
Use GPS and other tracking technologies for real-time monitoring of the cargo’s location and status throughout the journey.
Coordinate with the port of arrival to arrange for the cargo’s prompt unloading and handling.
Manage end-to-end transport in case of transhipment to ensure smooth transitions and avoid delays.
Ensure all necessary documentation for the handover is completed and the correct cargoes are delivered to the correct consignee/agent.
Retrieve/locate cargo from a storage location for delivery.
Verify labelling, condition of packaging, and the number of quantities against delivery orders.
Perform release of cargo to customer/agent.
Acknowledge the delivery order once the shipment is released to the correct consignee/agent.
Report any irregularity/ damage at the storage location and warehouse equipment and notify the superior.
Review the entire transport process to identify any issues or areas for improvement.
Coordinate for usage of cranes, lift trucks, or custom-built transportation equipment to load, secure for oversized or heavy loads, and unload the cargo.
Make sure that the cargo is physically inspected for any damage or discrepancies before and after transport to ensure it arrives in the expected condition.
Provide feedback and reports to all stakeholders, including clients, shipping companies/carriers, and port/ airport authorities.

modules.module_title: Manage the special cargo air movement

pcs.pc_description: Check the ULD contour and quality before acceptance of perishable cargo.
Ensure the agent utilises the correct ULD allotment.
Conduct quality checks on ULD serviceability and netting before handing them to the agent for the buildup of intact ULD at the Perishable Truck Dock.
Perform real-time tracking of vessels and cargo using carrier’s tracking systems/ GPS and AIS (Automatic Identification System).

modules.module_title: Administer the special cargo sea movement

pcs.pc_description: Coordinate with port authorities to ensure facilities and equipment meet requirements.
Maintain regular communication with the vessel’s crew, port authorities, and logistics managers to address any issues promptly.
Perform real-time tracking of vessels and cargo using carrier’s tracking systems/ GPS and AIS (Automatic Identification System).

modules.module_title: Manage the special cargo movement by road

pcs.pc_description: Determine the best route considering road limitations, weight restrictions, and potential obstacles. Specialised routes may be necessary for oversized or heavy loads.
Obtain the necessary permits for transporting special cargo, which can vary by region and cargo type, in compliance with local, national, and international regulations.
Coordinate with various stakeholders, including transportation providers, local authorities, and destination facilities, to ensure smooth movement and handling.
Use vehicles equipped for special cargo, such as flatbeds, lowboys for ODC, tankers for hazardous liquids or Armoured trucks for high- value shipments.

Ensure the safety protocols to protect the cargo and the transport team are followed, such as using escorts for oversized loads, following specific safety guidelines for hazardous materials, and having safety equipment available.

modules.module_title: Monitor the special cargo movement by rail

pcs.pc_description: Determine the most suitable rail route, considering factors like track capacity, bridge and tunnel restrictions, and the proximity of loading and unloading facilities. Special routes or schedules may be needed for oversized loads.
Coordinate timing to ensure rail transport aligns with specialised railcars and equipment availability. Some types of special cargo may require dedicated trains or priority scheduling.
Use railcars designed for special cargo, such as flatcars for oversized items, tank cars for liquids, or refrigerated cars for perishable goods.
For extremely heavy or oversized loads, use custom-built railcars or specialised equipment, such as crane cars, for loading and unloading.

modules.module_title: Handle exceptions during special air cargo reservations

pcs.pc_description: Resolve issues related to documents like SLI (Shipper’s Letter of Instruction), packing list, certificate of origin, commercial invoice, customs approval to export (let export) and other relevant documents (e.g., UN specification packaging, hazard labels, and markings).
Provide specialised advice over and above the system database, TACT Rules and applicable manuals to ensure that the shipment is permitted to be carried without any restrictions or limitations.
Ensure such changes are carried out with the least inconvenience to customers and operational requirements in case of severe disruption, which requires mass initiation of changes in the booking.

Liaise with capacity optimisation to assist the case where possible a shipment is queued to capacity optimisation for confirmation, which requires additional attention due to special and/or unique circumstances.

Assess the authenticity and appropriateness of the weight data provided, and evidence of such information needs to be placed on record for future queries in case of out-of-gauge, huge package/s and other cases.

Escalate cases where special circumstances require the application of rate/charges, including other applicable charges such as Terminal Storage and Processing Charges (TSP), documentation away from the published information.

modules.module_title: Manage special cargo and special products with unique requirements

pcs.pc_description: • Ensure that when multiple special product/cargo types are involved, the below are checked • • use of appropriate product/handling code/s • • assessment and application of appropriate charges • • insertion of appropriate remarks/instructions to the stakeholders/regulatory authorities
Follow up while shipment is in transit and ensure that such special products/cargo are handled in an appropriate manner.
Assess the situation and take appropriate decisions related to special products/cargo and address complexities.
Make advance arrangements related to special cargo/special products as and when they arise towards resolution or escalation.
Keep check on all the special cargo/product- related documents to ensure their smooth acceptance, transportation and delivery.
Initiate the necessary process towards securing additional regulatory/organisation approval when appropriate and guide the customer when external approvals are involved.
Liaise with the capacity optimisation unit in specific challenging cases related to the type of special cargo/product.

Escalate for pending issues warranting reassessment of the applicable rate/charges, including other applicable charges such as Terminal Storage and Processing Charges (TSP), documentation as per the tariff provided by the pricing section.

modules.module_title: Complying with National and International regulations and safety standards.

pcs.pc_description: Ensure compliance with customs regulations for importing and exporting special cargo, including declarations and inspections.
Adhere to the specific regulations governing the transport of special cargo, including national standards for cargo securing, documentation, and safety protocols.
Follow specific port and airport regulations for handling, loading, and unloading special cargo.
Comply with regulations and guidelines from regulatory bodies such as IATA (e.g. Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR) & Cargo Handling Manual (CHM), ICAO and AAI for special cargo movement by air.
Ensure that documents such as BOL, DG declaration, Certificates of Compliance, Insurance Certificates, Special Permits, and Hazardous Cargo Permits are received in advance and filed appropriately.
Comply with regulations regarding cargo securing and loading, e.g. SOLAS.

Make certain that environmental regulations, including proper disposal of hazardous materials and adherence to MARPOL (International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships) standards, are followed.
Identify potential risks that may arise while transporting special cargo, such as transit delays, equipment failure, safety hazards, theft, non- compliance with regulations, etc.

Recognise distinctive risks related to specific special Cargo, like weight distribution and secure handling for Oversized or Heavy Cargo; risks of leaks, spills, or exposure to toxic substances; risks of spoilage or damage due to temperature fluctuations for perishable goods; risks of theft and sabotage of high-value shipments, etc.
Assess each identified risk's potential impact and probability and consider historical data, industry benchmarks, and expert opinions.
Check the availability of SOPs and preventive methods for the risks identified.
Propose management for creating SOPs and preventive methods in case they are unavailable.
Monitor the implementation of the SOPs and prevention methods.
Maintain records of risks and near-miss incidents and report to management.

pcs.pc_description: Adhere to safety processes according to the different locations (cargo loading area, ramp operation area, etc.) in the area of operation.
Wear appropriate PPE specific to the area of operations and consider the goods being handled, such as goggles, earplugs, helmets, masks, shoes, etc.
Adhere to hazard communication protocols and infer safety data sheets (SDS) and warning signs.
Maintain a clean and organised work environment free of clutter and potential hazards.
Report any unsafe work conditions or practices immediately to DG Experts or safety personnel.
Follow emergency response plans and procedures for various scenarios (e.g., leaks, fires, equipment failures).
Assist colleagues during emergency evacuations, ensuring everyone follows established routes and assembly points.
Participate in regular emergency response drills and training, demonstrating competence and composure in simulated scenarios.
Undertake periodical preventive health check ups.
Follow security procedures like green gate in port, customs area, factory security, etc.
Adhere to standard safety procedures while handling hazardous/fragile cargo and walk only on the designated pathway.
Check if material handling procedures are being followed according to special cargo being handled and stacking is done accordingly.
Verify if all the safety and security-related tags, labels and signage are placed in the cargo.
Act immediately during emergencies and move to safety.
Provide first aid to affected victims, e.g., in case of bleeding, burns, choking, electric shock, poisoning etc.
In case of fire, follow fire safety practices taught during fire drills.
Follow procedures to rescue victims of fire without endangering themselves.
